newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: University rector resigns, meets student demands.
newsitem.headline: University rector resigns, meets student demands.

text.p: Belgrade University Rector Dragutin Velickovic resigned on Friday, meeting a demand by his students who ended a 106-day protest against election fraud in Serbia earlier in the day.
"Now that my demand for the students to return to classes has been fuflfilled... I am tendering my resignation," the rector told state media.

Belgrade students on Wednesday offered to end their marathon protest and return to classes on Friday if Velickovic stepped down. The rector had said he would resign only when students returned to classes.
With no solution to marathon protest in sight, university deans loyal to the students pressed them on Wednesday to test Velickovic's promise by returning to their faculties.

The student protests continued even after the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition ended three months of mass demonstrations in February after Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic restored opposition local election victories in 14 cities which his ruling socialist party (SPS) had annulled in November.
The widespread protests were the biggest challenge to Milosevic's 10-year rule.
